doc.title: Ametria Dock interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 4, 2019

title: Joe Williams and the hated headset microphones
summary: Prompted by Joe Williams working a handheld mic, Dock says she hates headset mics and in-ears because they emphasize performance over vocal work.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: You said something that reminded me of Joe Williams, who I explained had a big role in what we’re doing here. You said, “Sometimes she wants me to pull back.” And we filmed him once in a concert in our hall here, and there’s this moment there where he was singing a ballad and the Count Basie Band is behind him. And he took the microphone, and the microphone was at belt level, right? And he was singing but he was using that microphone to his good effect. And then I thought about a lot of singers nowadays, I see them with these little mics that come down on their cheek. What’s your feeling about those things?

I hate those microphones. I hate those microphones and I hate in-ears. I love being able to connect with your audience. The microphones that are here are restricting, honestly. And most of the time when they have those type of mics it’s because they’re doing dance routines and things like that and so they have those mics to not be restricted in that way. But it’s still, again, the emphasis is more on the performance and less on vocally what you’re doing. And so sometimes you have the stems playing in the background so you don’t have to work as hard as a singer. So they’ll have the actual vocal playing and they’re dancing, and their focus is more on the performance and less on you singing.
It seems to be you’re putting more emphasis on the sound person. You know what I’m trying to say? You can’t sing full out but go back from the mic.
Right, right. Go back from the mic. But here you don’t have that option so they have to run something through the system because you’re technically not singing really.
